body.objective: Determine whether the exact finite two-angle apparatus Hamiltonian is the compression of a spatially local microscopic scalar detector coupling, and classify any unavoidable leakage to other angles.
activates: an explicit local quadratic derivative density with opposite weights on the rational c=0 and c=3/5 pair modes
a Hermitian two-quadrature detector coupling for arbitrary relative phase
an exact selected-sector pair-absorption Hamiltonian compression
a decision whether finite-derivative locality can make the two-angle carrier invariant in the continuum
body.current_gate: Evaluate :phi^2: and :(partial_y phi)^2: between the vacuum and both exact pair modes. Construct D_minus=:phi^2:-(625/[72 kappa^2]):(partial_y phi)^2: and prove its relative weights are +1,-1. Combine D_plus=:phi^2: and D_minus in two real pointer quadratures to obtain phase weights (1,-exp(-i phi))/sqrt(2). Then prove or refute exact two-angle selectivity for any compactly smeared finite-derivative local quadratic density on the continuous fixed-energy angle family.
body.stop_condition: Land an exact CLASSIFIED local-compression/no-go certificate, method-distinct verifier, mutation tests, report and Papers 05/06 update. Separate exact selected-sector compression from full microscopic evolution and state leakage as open unless invariance is proved.
body.forbid: no equality of compressed Hamiltonians promoted to equality of full exponentials; no local vertex called an invariant detector sector; no finite-angle reduced result promoted to continuum locality, public BT evolution, Eq. 19, gravity, QME or LORENTZIAN-CAUSAL physics
body.resource_hint: For the rational outgoing pairs, -k1_y k2_y/kappa^2 is 0 at c=0 and 144/625 at c=3/5. Hence D_minus has weights 1 and 1-(625/72)(144/625)=-1. With D_plus weights (1,1), alpha=(1-exp(-i phi))/(2 sqrt(2)) and beta=(1+exp(-i phi))/(2 sqrt(2)) give alpha D_plus+beta D_minus weights (1,-exp(-i phi))/sqrt(2). On the fixed-total-momentum continuum, compact smearing is common to all angles and a finite-derivative density restricts to a finite Laurent polynomial in exp(i theta); it cannot vanish on the open complement of two angles without vanishing identically.
